# Test 20261006-130630-53bb: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:5; app.py:27; app.py:59; state.json:14 | `shop.refund` received `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `{"refund": "RF-4BB0A4", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}`. The rule says, “A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it.” The code sets `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000` but compares `args["amount_eur"] > APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS`, so €80 bypassed approval and was saved under the order's `refunds`. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:13; trace.jsonl:17; app.py:64; app.py:67 | The app promised the refund “will appear on your card shortly” and repeated in turn 3 that it was “heading to your card.” The tool returns a refund ID, amount, and `"status": "paid"`; its implementation only saves a local refund record. Neither the result nor the rules establishes a card destination, a card payment, or settlement timing. |

## Notes

The seal is intact: no test record changed after the test ended. Reviewed all three transcript turns and all 18 trace items, findings.json, audit.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, and the current state.json using read-only commands. Findings are empty; the audit reports no altered exchanges, breaks, errors, or blocked calls.

The current state contains the exact refund ID `RF-4BB0A4` and amount €80 for order 5120, with no approval queue. The order lookup and refund amount match the tester's request, and the completion replies agree with the local paid-refund state; that state itself violates the manager-approval rule. The card assurance above is one issue repeated across turns 2 and 3.

No project tests or additional specifications were present in the file inventory. Delivery dates and external card settlement could not be verified from the available records or state. No app was started, no message was sent, and no state was changed; only this report was written.
